articleTitle: Progress in optical recording at 428nm
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. Experiments demonstrating high density optical recording at 428 nm using the recently developed compact, frequency doubled diode laser and optimized COPT multilayer media are described.

articleTitle: Data storage using scanning probe microscopes

publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993

articleTitle: Optical storage - The customer's perspective

articleTitle: Stimulating demand for optical storage
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. Optical storage technologies have proven themselves. Producibility has been confirmed. Why, then, hasn't demand become stronger? The factors gating market demand are examined, and projected levels of demand and pricing are presented.

articleTitle: Sb Induced Stable Cluster Structures Of Ge-Sb-Te Phase Change Optical Memory Materials
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993

articleTitle: 3.5" MO for personal systems
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993

articleTitle: Thermodynamic Simulation Of Magnetic Field Modulation Methods For Pulsed Laser Irradiation In Magneto-optical Disks
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Direct overwrite magnetic field modulation with dc and pulsed laser irradiation methods in magneto-optical disk is simulated thermodynamically. Since the focused laser beam heats the magnetic film to allow the magnetization to be reversed, the waveform of the laser beam strongly affects the shape of the magnetic domain. The dynamic temperature changes in magnetic thin films are simulated for dc and pulse laser irradiations. With pulse irradiation, the heat is constrained to within a limited local area, which results in jitter-free magnetic domains, high optical efficiency, and high TPI as well as high BPI recording.

articleTitle: Multirate Sampling Digital Servo Of An Optical Disk Drive
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Full digital implementation of disk drive electronics is expected to improve the performance of drives as well as to reduce their cost, power consumption, and form factor. The Digital Signal Processor (DSP) has recently been used as a servo controller for optical disk drives. Although DSP implementation has the advantage of flexibility, the servo control algorithm has to be simple so that it can finish the computation within a specified time interval. The sampling rate is determined by the servo bandwidth, and is about ten times higher than that of a hard disk drive. Therefore, conventional microprocessors cannot be used in optical disk drives and an efficient algorithm is always necessary for DSP servo.

articleTitle: Video-on-demand System Architecture Using An Optical Mass Storage System
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Video-on-demand (VOD) systems, using the communication network to send requested video programs from video storage centers to terminals, are applicable to services such as movies, commodities-guides, and video museums. Against the background of digitization of communications and progress in video compression techniques, digital VOD has recently been proposed [1,2]. The volume of digital video data, however, is enormous: about 1.1 GB per 100 minutes even at the 1.5 Mbps of the IS0 MPEG standard. The storage of many video programs therefore requires an optical mass storage system (MSS) [3], the use of which is associated with the following problems: (1)Response is slow because of the time required for mounting a disk. (2)When a video program divided into several surfaces or disks, the playback is interrupted while turning over or changing disks, and it is difficult to implement visual search. (3)Waiting time is long when all drives are in use. This paper proposes solutions for these problems and verifies their effectiveness in trial VOD system.

articleTitle: CD-R Interchangeability Test Report
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The "Orange Book part IV)", which describes technical specifications of CD-WO (Compact Disc Write Once,so-called CD-R), was released by Philips and Sony in November 1990. The CD-R (CD recordab1e)User Group was formed in August 1991 by 18 companies, both from disc manufacturers and hardware manufacturers, whose aim is to confirm interchangeability between discs and devices and eventually extract problems if any. This report introduces the activities of Test Group A in which 8 disc suppliers and 9 disc evaluators participated. The characteristics of CD-R discs and the interchangeability will be discussed.

articleTitle: Optical Recording System In Minidisc
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The MiniDisc (MD) system includes a recordable magneto-optical. (MO) disc for user-recording and a conventional read-only disc for music-software publishing. By means of audio data compression and shock resistant memory, MiniDisc is highly suited for outdoor portable applications.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study On High Data Transfer Rate Of 300 Mbit/s With 8-beam Laser Diode Array
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: An optical disk drive with a high date transfer rate is strongly desired for multimedia data storage.1) However, the data transfer rate of conventional drives is still low. Our study aims to raise the data transfer rate of an optical disk drive by more than ten times using multibeam recording. This paper shows experimental results at a high data transfer rate of 300 Mbit/s, the servo control and signal processing technologies necessary for a multibeam recording optical disk drive.

articleTitle: Write Control Method For High Density Magneto-optical Dim System
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Toward the product of first generation magnet-optical disk, the recording technique using the mark position recording method has been developed, by which the density of 400Mb/in² is attained. In order to increase the density.the technique combined with the mark edge recording method and zoned CAV method is suitable. In the write-once optical disk system of 12" size this technique has been first adopted and the density of 550Mb/in² is realized[l]. In the case of magnet-optical media the control of recording mark edge position and shape which is important for the mark edge recording method is hardly realized because of its higher thermal conductivity. Moreover, this characteristics is sensitive against the environmental temperature.

articleTitle: High Density Phase-change Optical Disk System Having Write And Read Compatibility With 90mm MO Disk
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: An optical disk system has been widely used, especially after the introduction of a 90mm magneto-optical (MO) disk meeting the Is0 standardization. Optical disk shall play the leading role in multi-media applications. On multi-media applications overwrite capability is indispensable. Phase-change (PC) optical recording technology has a feature to realize overwrite function only by the optical means, such as a write-once optical head. A 130mm 1 GB PC rewritable multifunction optical disk system was introduced in the market in early 1992. (1) This paper presents the high density recording characteristics of a PC optical disk and a 256MB 90mm overwritable PC optical disk system with full compatibility with a conventional MO disk.

articleTitle: Premastered Optical Disk By Superresolution
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Superresolution in reading out of optical disks expands the optical spatial cut­ off frequency, which is limited by the numerical aperture (NA) of the objective lens and the wavelength of the light source. Magnetically induced Super Resolution (MSR) was achieved for practical use in magneto-optical disks using exchange-coupled magnetic multi-layer film. The superresolution was extended to the readout of nonlinear disks which differ from magneto-optical disk. The theoretical importance, however, was stressed since the obtained carrier to noise (C/N) ratio of 34 dB at the cut-off frequency was too small for practical use. Now, we have achieved superresolution for practical use in a read-only system using a Ge2Sb2Te5 layer film. We call this newly developed technique Premastered optical disk by Super-Resolution (PSR). In this paper, we describe the principle and the experimental performance of PSR in detail.

articleTitle: Progress In Photorefractive Holographic Storage
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The possibility of implementing holographic memories taking advantage of the photorefractive effect has been proposed about 20 years ago and, since then, has been often demonstrated.

articleTitle: Holographic Optical Memory Architectures Based On Switchable Holograms
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Three dimensional optical data storage is of interest because of the potential for terabit/cubic centimeter capacities and gigabidsecond access rates. Although 3D storage could be either holographic or bit-oriented, holographic architectures have advantages of distributed recording for lower error rates and massively parallel read/write. However, two barriers have limited progress in the “sugar cube” approach to holographic memory. First, relatively few volume materials are appropriate for erasable real time holography, although a wider variety of thin film holographic materials are available. Second, most schemes require complex interface devices such as scanners, parallel read heads and dynamic lenses which are still under development.

articleTitle: A Repetitive Track Seek Algorithm For Optical Disk Drives
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: As is well known, lots of servo technologies for the optical disk drive system have been presented. The floating servo mechanism and the position error integration servo method, which were proposed by Inada et al., have played an important role in a high speed and accurate position control realization. In this paper, a repetitive track seek algorithm to carry out stable and high speed track seek motion is presented. The algorithm is realized through the velocity error integration. And the simulation results are also shown.

articleTitle: Response Properties Of A Liquid Crystal Microlens And Its Application To An Optical Head
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Recently, a basic experiment for applying a liquid crystal micro­ lens to an optical head has been reported, where the power of the microlens could be controlled by applying a relatively low voltage. In this report, the response properties of the liquid crystal micro­ lens, which are very important for applying the microlens to the opti­ cal head, are measured and their improvement is described based in the method of bias voltage application.

articleTitle: Multi-beam Read-verifying Optical Head For Parallel Recording
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Parallel data recording is a promising way to increase the data transfer rate of optical disks. Read-verifying after writing by using a multi-beam laser diode is also indispensable for high data transfer performance. This paper describes a multi-beam read-verifying optical head that uses a holographic beam splitter and a high-power visible laser diode.

articleTitle: Large-scale Holographic Memory: Experiment Results
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: We describe a holographic optical memory capable of storing up to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> bits of information. The stored in­formation is retrieved in blocks or pages, each consisting of 10³ x 10³ bits. Each page can be accessed randomly in approximately 100 μsec with an experimentally measured SNR of 816.8, and a projected probability of error of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-28</sup>.

articleTitle: 40mW Operation Of InGaalP Visible-light Laser Diodes
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: High power, 600nm wavelength range, InGaAlP visible-light laser diodes are key components for optical data storage systems. 30mW class visible­ light lasers for high density recording have been reported by several researchers. Higher power is desired for higher speed recording and larger allowances on pick-up head design. In this paper, we report on stable 40mW operation of InGaAlP laser diodes at 50°C, for the first time.

articleTitle: Measurement Of Domain Wall Mobility In magneto-optic media
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Weng and Kryder previously measured the minimum field pulse duration required to collapse domains in rare earth-transition metal films and estimated the domain wall velocity as the distance the domain wall had to travel to shrink the domain from its original diameter to the critical diameter at which it was no longer stable and would collapse due to the pressure from domain wall surface tension. Although the camera system they used to perform these experiments had been used to photograph dynamic processes in MO media, for measurements near the Curie temperature, the signal from the MO media became too weak to be observed. Hence they were not able to actually observe the dynamic collapse process, but had to rely upon observations before and after the field pulse was applied.

articleTitle: Volume Holographic Data Storage In Photo-organic Media
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Photo-organic media are promising for volume data storage because of low sample costs and easy fabrication of arbitrary sample shapes and sizes. The key disadvantage of volume data storage relative to planar storage is that the space-bandwidth product of the recording fields in a volume system must be large to achieve effective recording. This means that the cost of the data recording and reconstruction systems will be much higher. This problem is alleviated in cylindrical and spherical photo-organic storage media by eliminating the need for imaging optics.

articleTitle: Cached Magneto-optic Storage
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Magneto-Optic (MO) disk drives often display performance inferior to their magnetic counterparts, due to the high mass head/positioner and two pass write operation associated with MO. This paper will examine the effect of adding cache to an MO disk drive, and compare the result to a non-cached magnetic disk drive with equivalent capacity. First, traces of 130 000 disk requests under the popular Windows environment are collected. Second, the performance of MO and magnetic storage devices are characterized in a seek profile. Third, a trace driven simulation model is constructed to measure the effectiveness of 64KB to 8MB caches located in the disk drive controller. Finally, conclusions are drawn regarding the relationship between cache size and access time in the Windows environment.

articleTitle: Optimized Disk Structure And Ge-Te-Sb Composition For Overwritable Phase Change CD
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Phase change optical disk is suitable for rewritable compact disk (CD) system. Phase change optical disk has several advantages. for example it is easy to overwrite and can be read by using the same optical method as existing CD system. We investigated the disk structure and recording film composition suitable for low linear velocity, from the viewpoints of overwriting characteristics and reliability.

articleTitle: Effects Of A Shading Band In The Data Path Of An Optical Drive
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Efforts to improve the density of data recorded onto optical media have included shaping the function of the optical system. Several authors have described various methods for shaping th transfer e transfer function. Reference 1 contains a summary of the various techniques and plots of the transfer functions. In this paper, we describe the effects of a simple shading band in the data path of an optical drive. One effect of the shading band is to shape the transfer function of the optical system. This is similar to the technique of applying electronic equalizing filters for better frequency response. A second effect of the shading band is to decrease the noise associated with the laser and the medium. In our work, we implement a shading band in a commercial optical disk drive. The relevant parameters to this study are: shading band width = 30% of the pupil diameter, medium velocity = 5.7 m/s, NA = 0.55, and λ = 0.78 nm. We used a standard 130 mm magneto-optic disk with a plastic substrate. The following sections briefly describe the theory associated with using the shading band and the results of our experiments.

articleTitle: Advanced Direct Seeking System For 5.25" Magneto-optical Disk Drive
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: High speed accessing is very important feature of optical disk drive which could be used as the computer peripheral devices. In order to realize high speed accessing, various direct seeking system that a laser spot could get a target track directly without track jumping has been developed. In this paper, we described the newly developed direct seeking system which includes linearization method of tracking error signal for wider pull-in-range tracking servo system and two advanced detection methods, relative velocity detection method between a track and laser spot and distance detection method between present and target track.

articleTitle: The Write Laser Power Variation Contribution To Write Noise In MO Media
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Signal-to-Noise-Ratio (SNR) is an important indicator of performance in information storage systems. There are many components of noise in magneto-optical (MO) systems. Write noise, the additional noise created by writing on MO media, is an important element the total noise. Recently, several analytical models of write noise [1] were developed based on the assumption that it is caused by the variation in mark edge placement. The edge shift contribution to write noise has two components, an intrinsic media component, and a component caused by the variation in the write laser power. In this paper, power spectral density is used to "e the contribution of write laser power variation to total noise. The power spectrum is used to estimate the write laser power variation.

articleTitle: Intersymbol Interference Characterization And Equalization For High-density Optical Storage
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: In this paper, we study M-0 channel characteristics and use signal processing to achieve a higher storage density. Specifically, we recorded various data patterns and characterize the intersymbol interference (ISI) using a Nakamichi [2] M-0 drive. From the ISI characteristics, we use several equalization techniques to improve the SNR of readback signals. An improvement of 3-6 db is observed.

articleTitle: Improvement Of Track Density By Land And Groove Recording On Phase Change Optical Disk
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: In the past several years extensive studies have been carried out on the improvement of the recording density of rewritable optical disk.[1,2,3] However, these approaches need extra optical components, electrical circuits or disk layers. Thus, a desirable approach for high track density recording is to use conventional drives and disks without those extra components. We have realized this method of recording by introducing an optical phase difference for adjacent recording tracks to suppress cross-talk. The optical phase difference is introduced by the depth of a groove when signals are recorded on both the groove area and the land area. (See Fig. 1.) Recording on such areas can achieve twice the track density, compared to conventional systems. In this paper, we discuss the possibility of cross-talk suppression and doubling the track density from the view point of simulation and experimental results obtained by applying this recording method to a phase change optical disk.

articleTitle: Write-once Optical Disk Using Ge-Sb-Te/Bi-Te Bilayer Film For Mark-edge Recording
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: A high density recording was investigated by using a mark-edge recording method for AgTe-C hlm [l], where an ablative recording was carried out to form a pit. The tracking servo control was pointed out to be influenced by the decrease of reflectivity, which was brought about by the long length pits formed repeatedly. Ge-Sb-Te/Bi-Te write-once disk was developed as a nonablative type media, where data were recorded by the alloying process between the two layers, to keep the tracking servo control being stable. We will report the mark-edge recording characteristics and the reliability of the disk using an alloying process

articleTitle: Completely Erasable Phase Change Optical Disk II -application Of Ag-In-Sb-Te Mixed-phased System For CD-rewritable Compatible With CD1X And CD2X
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: As previously reported, phase change optical disk with our original recording material, Ag-In-Sb-Te mixed-phased system, exhibits excellent performance, such as complete erasure and high sensitivity.

articleTitle: The High Density Recording Characteristics Of A 90 Mm Phase Change Optical Disk
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: A phase change medium is promising as a future optical recording medium, because it can be ily adapted to a double sided disk, and a carrier to noise ratio (CNR) is high even when using eas a short wavelength laser diode as a light source. In this paper, CNR, erasability, and bit error rate (BER) of a 90 mm high density phase change optical disk are described. These are the parameters which show a reliability of a large 300 Mbytes capacity (single sided). The authors used a 0.6 mm thick disk and an optical head which had a 690 nm fast controlled laser diode!> and an objective lens with a large N.A. value of 0.6. This storage capacity is easily doubled (600 Mbytes) by joining two disks to form a double sided disk.

articleTitle: Evolution Of Optical Disk Era Into The 21st Century
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The commercialization of compact disk (CD) in 1982 was a landmark event in the evolution of optical disk. The compact disk has since enjoyed an overwhelming support from consumers who were not contented with LP records. More than 300 million disks and 50 million players were sold in 1992. Not only did the CD revolutionize world-wide audio market, the successful format standardization it brought on stimulated the software industry to switch from LP records to CD.

articleTitle: High Density PWM Recording And Rewritable Capability In The GeSbTe Phase Change System By Using Visual Laser Beam At Lower Linear Velocity
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Recently, the investigations on optical media are being done for the high density recording and/or one beam overwrite in magneto-optical[ 1,2] and phase change[3,4] systems. Phase change type optical media are promising candidates for visual laser beam recording because of its easy tunable optical properties for irradiating light.

articleTitle: A Near-field Scanning Optical Microscope For Analysis Of Magneto-optic Media
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The ability to achieve subwavelength optical resolution for microscopy through the use of a mechanically scanned near-field optical probe has recently been reported.¹ This technique provides a means of exceeding the far-field diffraction limit associated with the use of an objective lens in conventional optical microscopy, and is known as near-field scanning optical microscopy (NSOM). The near-field probe may be realized by forming a subwavelength-sized aperture in an opaque screen. Such a probe may be implemented in practice by tapering an optical fiber down to the desired diameter and coating its exterior (except for the very tip) with aluminum. The spatial resolution achieved is dependent on the aperture diameter and the tip-to­ sample separation, and the resolution is approximately equal to the aperture diameter for separations less than one aperture radius.

articleTitle: Motionless-head Parallel Readout Optical Disk Prototype System
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The design, analysis and experimental demonstration of the motionless-head parallel readout optical disk system are presented. The system is designed to read 1-D data blocks distributed radially on the disk’s active surface and generate 2-D output binary images. It has the unique advantage that no mechanical motion of the head is required for fast access, focusing or tracking. This allows a data rate of up to 1 Gbyte/sec for standard disk rotation speeds of 2400 rpm.

articleTitle: Latest Developments Of Components For An Integrated Magneto-optical Head
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: LETI (Optronics and Microelectronics Departments) is involved in an European project (ESPRIT 2013) dealing with magneto-optical recording. In order to build a flying magneto-optical integrated head (figure 1), LETI has developed two basic components: - a reading and focusing integrated optical circuit connected to optical fibers - a thin film magnetic circuit (to generate the perpendicular magnetic field for writing purposes) which should be monolithically implanted onto the optical circuit and electrically connected. Integrated optics [1] and magnetics on silicon bring the advantages of integration such as weight and size reduction, better reliability, mass production and low cost possibility, and allow for a high modulation frequency of the magnetic field. Therefore, a magneto-optical disk drive, using this integrated head, has enough winning cards like direct overwriting, short access time, high data transfer rate, to be competitive with other systems. Two years ago, we demonstrated the feasibility of a reading integrated optical circuit [2] by using a simplified test circuit, of larger size, fiberless connection and without integration of the thin film magnetic coil. In this paper, we present the final circuits, the association of both technologies and the experimental results obtained on the different components.

articleTitle: High Density Video Disc Using Superresolution And Green Laser
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: In order to achieve higher definition, longer playing and smaller disc diameter optical video discs, it is essential to improve recording density. It is reported that making wavelength shorter by using SHG and adopting super resolution technique are effective means to accomplish this. As for high density optical disc system using short wavelength SHG green laser, few reports on 90-minute MUSE disc system has been made.2>³> It is our subject in hand to develop a single sided High-Vision disc with a diameter of 300mm which can play for 2 hours, or a CD size double-sided NTSC disc with a diameter of 120mm which can play for 1 hour per both, as one of our product targets. This paper describes the optical head using super resolution and green laser, and the high density video disc with 2 hours of playback time per side.

articleTitle: A Complete Study Of Differential Wax-wane Focus Servo Technique
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: We concentrate on differential wax-wane focus servo technique that is insensitive to many of the errors found in other schemes. Servo optics are illustrated in Figure 1. The beam reflected from optical disk is focused by the detector lens onto two detectors, detector 1 is slightly inside focus, and detector 2 is slightly beyond focus. The quad detector is offset from the center of the beam to give the FES algebra, where a is an electronic gain factor that can be any number larger than one.

articleTitle: The Performance Of A 600 Mbyte 90 Mm Phase Change Optical Disk Against Disk Tilt
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Package memories with a large capacity of about 600 Mbytes (equivalent to CD-ROMs) and an overwrite function are required in order to store compressed digital video signals for multi-media applications. A phase change optical disk is suitable for such applications because a high C/N ratio is easily attainable under an overwrite operation.

articleTitle: Magneto-optic Head Using Substrate-mode Grating Pairs For Polarization And Leaky Beamsplitting
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: In a magneto-optic data storage system, polarization and leaky beamsplitting ele­ ments are required in the optical pickup head.¹ The polarization beamsplitting element is used to sense the rotation of the beam polarization reflected from the magneto-optic disc medium. The leaky beamsplitter in conjunction with a half-wave plate is used to enhance the differential signal level detected from the medium. Conventionally, bulk prisms are used as polarization and leaky beamsplitters. In our novel substrate-mode grating pair structure, both functions can be performed.

articleTitle: Rapid Access Method For OpticaI Disk Drive Using Feedforward Brake Pulse
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Access operation of optical disk drive is divided into macro-seeking, micro-seeking, and tracking at a destination track. A two-stage actuator system consisting of an object lens actuator, OLA, and a linear motor. LM, is commonly employed for the tracking servo system of an optical disk drive. The OLA is, however, stationary during macro-seeking. A rapid access method using the two-stage actuator system more actively is discussed.

articleTitle: Integrated-optic Focus Spot Intensity Modulator For Disc Head
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Implementation of integrated-optic (IO) pickup heads would result in great improvements in reduction of size, weight, and number of fabrication processes as well as in application flexibility in optical memory systems. Several IO pickups [1-3] have been proposed and demonstrated by the authors for read-only optical discs, magneto-optical discs or optical cards. In this paper, we propose a new IO device modulating focus spot intensity and demonstrate preliminary experimental results for a future application to an IO writing/reading head used in rewritable disc systems. Following the IO pickups previously reported [1-3], the IO modulator is constructed in a slab waveguide on a Si substrate because of its advantages such as excellent flatness, possibility of monolithic integration of photodiodes, compatibility with the IO pickups, low cost, etc. In order to modulate the focus spot intensity for writing data on the disc, electro-optic (EO) modulation is required provided grating components are used in the IO device, since power modulation of laser diode (LD) causes wavelength fluctuation which should be avoided because the gratings have wavelength dispersion. An EO polymer film is used as a guiding layer for the EO modulation because of its fabrication easiness. Although the material is not currently well-chosen and the fabrication process not well-established, we have investigated IO-EO switching devices [4,5] integrating grating couplers and electrodes in a slab waveguide consisting of an EO polymer on a Si substrate. Device configuration A schematic view of the proposed IO focus spot modulator is shown in Fig. 1. The IO device is constructed by integrating a focusing grating coupler (FGC) and poling/modulating electrodes in a slab waveguide on a Si substrate. The waveguide is made of a poled p-NAn-PVA (p-nitroaniline n-polyvinyl alcohol) [6] guiding layer, a polymer (OEBRlOO) upper- and a SiO2 lower-buffer layers, and is sandwiched by planar Au and Au/Cr films (see Fig. 2) which are used as poling electrodes as well as modulating electrodes. The FGC consists of corrugation of Si-N layer deposited on the lower buffer layer and couple a guided wave diverging from a butt-coupled LD to a free-space beam focusing to a point on a disc. The upper electrodes are separated to two parts (interdigital configuration with 4 fingers is shown in Fig. 1). By applying modulation signal to one of the upper electrodes, we can modulate a phase retardation of the guided wave under the one part electrode against the wave under the other part. The intensity distribution of the FGC focus spot along the lateral direction changes according to the phase retardation. The examples are shown in Fig. 2 for the cases of two fingers and three fingers electrodes. As the retardation increases up to 1t, the center peak reduces and other peaks grow. An extinction ratio may be defined by the ratio of the center peak intensity in on-state to the highest peak (no matter which the highest peak is) intensity in off-state. The maximum extinction ratio is 3 dB for two fingers case and becomes higher when the number of fingers is larger.

articleTitle: Newly Packaged 50-pm-spaced 8-element Las;er Diode Array With A Thermoelectzic Emler
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Although a dense array of individually addressable high-power laser diode elements can increase the data transfer rate of optical disk drives, the junction temperature rise - including thermal interaction between elements - shortens array lifetime and affects the elements' operating characteristics. Here we report that reliable operation can nonetheless be achieved by adjusting the array cavity length and by using a copper package that incorporates a thermoelectric cooler.

articleTitle: Polarization Issues In Magneto-optic Media And Head
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Polarization of light plays an important role in magneto-optical recording. The birefringence present in plastic substrates can cause complications not only in readout of the magneto-optical data, but also in focusing and tracking servo signals. In this paper we describe some of the problems associated with substrate birefringence and also discuss the interaction of polarized light with grooved structures.

articleTitle: Future Trends In Frequency-seiective Optical Memories
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The scheme of frequency selective hole burning memories was invented about 15 years ago /1/ and has caused world wide activities /2/ in the search for realizing a prototype memory which would be suited for technical implementation. In our view such an implementation has so far not been achieved due to the following reasons:

articleTitle: Crosstalk Analysis Of GaAlAs Laser Arrays
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: There has been considerable interest recently in the application of laser arrays to optical data storage. Performance enhancements that are possible include Direct-Read-After-Write or Direct-Overwrite using a 2-element array, increased track density using parallel read with a 3-element array, and high-data-rate parallel recording with an array of n lasers. One of the major considerations is the spacing of the lasers in the array. A large spacing makes laser packaging easier but puts demands on the optical system : large flat field, control of vignetting, etc. As the spacing is reduced, however, crosstalk between the clements will increase, and a large factor in determining the optimum spacing will be the maximum allowable crosstalk.

articleTitle: Scanning Laser Microscopy Of Magneto-optic Storage Media
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Scanning laser microscopy provides a most powerful tool for the investigation of magneto-optic storage media and systems. Not only can fundamental properties, such as Kerr rotation, reflectivity, coercivity, hysteresis loop shape of the storage material itself be investigated, but a quantitative measure of recording and overwrite performance can be obtained. Furthermore, the evaluation of important record/replay system parameters such as noise performance and read head resolution is straightforward. Finally, the Scanning laser microscope (SLM) provides an ideal instrument base with which to investigate novel record and replay methods, such as direct overwrite and phase contrast and super-resolution read techniques.

articleTitle: Edge Shift Characteristics Of A Magneto-optical Edge Detection Signal
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: With the recent mark edge recording method, various methods have been proposed for reducing the intersymbol interference which occurs on making the capacity bc in high density in the magneto-optical(M0) disk. But few proposals have been made on the optical edge detection system of the MO disks. We have studied a MO edge readout system. The system optically processes diffraction wavefronts from the MO edges within a diffraction limited spot, and detects edges from their intensity distributions. We estimated the readout edge signal experimentally by measuring frequency response of a carrier to noise ratio and a edge shift characteristics.

articleTitle: Hybrid Achromatic Objective Lens Design For Optical Data Storage
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: As higher power laser diodes are incorporated into optical data storage systems, wavelength shifts of several nanometers can occur between read and write powers, which demands that some attention be given to the chromatic correction of the optical system. This paper presents the design of a hybrid objective lens that is chromatically corrected by the addition of a diffractive element to the second surface of the lens. It is low mass, small size, and provides high Strehl Ratio performance. A 0.47 N.A. hybrid objective lens corrected for monochromatic aberrations has been discussed previously by Goto et al.

articleTitle: Read Laser Power Effects In Magneto-optic Data Recording
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Implementation and effectiveness of optical super-resolution and optical edge detection techniques depends crucially on the optical transfer function of the objective lens and media combination. This paper demonstrates effects of read-out laser power on the read-back signal from Kerr effect media. Experimental results are compared to calculations based on an oversimplified model of thermal behavior and domain geometry. The results indicate that these effects, although noticable, are of small importance for pulse width modulation recording based on standard optical systems.

articleTitle: CD-i, The Individualized Execution Of Programs/titles And Storage Requirements
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Consumer interactivity with a Multi Media-system is a balance between Linear Play and actual Interactivity. This balance is different for TV-viewing, where interactivity means "zapping", and for CD-i use: CD-i fulfils more individual requirements. Within this trend, CD-i related definitions and requirements towards even more individualized performance is analysed and explained within the overall CD-i principles.

articleTitle: Pre-recorded Signal Characteristics Of High Density Optical Disks
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: To increase the capacity has become essential to optical disks. Recently, many ideas of recording technique for increasing the recording density have been proposed. For the performance of the high density disks, the quality of the pre-recorded and servo signals is very important in rewritable disks as well as fully read-only disks (0-ROM) or partially read-only disks (P-ROM).

articleTitle: Recording And Erasing Characteristics At A Wavelength Of 680nm For A Phase Change Disk Designed For 830nm Wavelength
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Morimoto et al. have reported that a phase change optical film showed more than 10% reflectivity change over a wide range of wavelengths from 400 to 900nm. This means that some phase change optical materials are practical for high density recording because short wavelength lasers are necessary to create small laser spots. This paper discusses exchangeability regarding laser wavelength and mark size.

articleTitle: 2.5 Inch Flat-type Phase-change Optical Disk Drive
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: A 2.5 inch flat-type, phase-change optical disk drive of 15mm in height has been developed to be mounted into a notebook-type personal computer. In order to thin down the drive height we developed a 0.6mm polycarbonate substrate, phase-change type optical disk materials, and a 6mm height thin-type optical head.

articleTitle: Read Channel And Format For High Densrry Magneto-optical Disk System
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The read/write technologies for a second generation of magneto-optical disk are developed. Regarding the request for second generation, a large capacity 1GB on 130mm size disk and higher transfer-rate faster than 2MB/s are required. Therefore mark length recording method and zoned CAV method are applied for the first time. Required recording density is 880Mbit/in. In this paper, the concept of developed system, especially read channel and its characteristics are reported. That is, modulation scheme, disk format, read out method, detection method are signal processing. This concept is proven by read/write experiment.

articleTitle: In-Ag-Te-Sb Phase Change Recording Media At CD Linear Velocity
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Many applications of phase change recording media have been reported so far. It has been very interesting to apply phase change recording media to rewritable CD. Te-Ge-Sb ternary alloy is one of the most investigated materials as phase change recording media. Ohno et al.(l) applied the alloy film to rewritable CD by controlling the composition to decrease the crystallization speed.

articleTitle: High Density Optical Disk Systent U9m Variable Five Modulation And Shg Green Laser
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: A higher density optical disk system is very attractive for computer data storage, audio and video applications. We have realized the readout of optical disks with a 6 time higher areal density than that of conventional CDs (compact discs).

articleTitle: Future Generation MO Media From A Manufacturing Point Of View
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: MO media technology is now on the first step of mass production. For a "Big Bang" of MO industry, we should add more fascinating points for users. The first priority is to realize low cost technology. Cost consists of materials, throughput and yield. The second priority is to achieve a large memory capacity using techniques like a mark edge recording, short wavelength lasers, magnetic super resolutions (MSR) and so on. High speed capability is also important. Especially, MO disk requires an overwriting capability. For future generation MO disk, a lot of schemes are proposed and attract many researchers. Here, I'll try to check such schemes from an above mentioned point of view.

articleTitle: Modelling thermal diffusion of scanned and focused laser power on direct overwrite magneto-optical disk
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: For high data density recording with mark edge recording, for example, 0.56 μm/bit which has been proposed for the next generation standard (NGS) Magneto-Optical (MO) disk, thermal interference in forming mark edges should be pre compensated [1] or should be made uniform (i.e. not dependent on the data pattern recorded on the disk). Meanwhile, direct overwrite (DOW) is an indispensable function for the NGS MO disk for rewritable multi-media applications [2]. We, therefore, report that thermal diffusion of scanned and focused laser power on DOW-MO disk could be analyzed with a simplified analytical model which has three main fitting parameters, the specific heat: Cp [J/°C ·m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>], the thermal diffusivity: [m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/sec], and the adiabatic index: n [anonymous dimensionless] of the resin sandwiching both the dielectric and MO thin film constituting the DOW-MO disk. The model is useful to predict the thermal interference in forming mark edges on the DOW-MO disk.

articleTitle: Optical Head With Annular Phase-shifting Apodizer
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: An annular phase-shifting optical element (annular apodizer) with super-resolution characteristics, to be implemented in read/write heads for optical discs, was theoretically proposed by one of the authors'). To confirm the theoretical analysis, the annular apodizer was experimentally fabricated with the lift-off method, and 18@degree phase shift was realized for 780nm transferred light. In this report, the superior optical characteristics of the annular apodizer, like intensity profile sharpening and focal depth enlarging, are shown by using both experimental results and computer simulation.

articleTitle: Thin Injection Molded Substrate For High Density Recording Phase Change Retritable Optical Disk
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: First-generation phase change rewritable and MO optical disks have been commercialized. There are two approaches to high density optical recording. One is by applying shorter wavelength laser diodes. The second is using a large NA optical lens. Larger-NA optics are sensitive to disk tilt characteristics because of aberrations in the disk substrate. We propose a thin disk substrate to give wide disk tilt tolerance. This article will deal with the characteristics of thin injection molded polycarbonate disk substrate and crosstalk characteristics of phase change rewritable optical disks using large-NA optics.

articleTitle: Durability Of Writable CD Media
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: A CD audio or CD-ROM disc consists of an injection molded polycarbonate substrate, with the information represented as depressions, coated with an aluminum or aluminum alloy reflective layer. A polymeric layer (the “lacquer”) is coated on the reflector to protect it. Each layer adheres reasonably well to the other, resulting in a rugged package. This reputation for ruggedness has led to rather cavalier handling of these discs by consumers.

articleTitle: Adaptive Head Positioning Using Multiple Beams
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: A highly precise head positioning technique is important to the successful development of optical disk components for high-density storage systems. This paper reports on a new head positioning technique in which multiple beams with minute offsets (Δx) between them are employed diagonally across the data track. Data tracking involves selecting among these offset beams.

articleTitle: Improvement In Jitter Characteristics In Mark Edge Recording For Phase Change Media
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Mark edge recording (MER) is effective in achieving higher recording density. However, whether MER can be applied to phase change media has yet to be sufficiently investigated. In this study, we have analyzed the factors dominating jitter characteristics and shown how jitter in MER can be reduced.

articleTitle: 3-D Holographic Disks
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The 3-D holographic disk [l] (HD) is shown in Fig. 1. It consists of a photosensitive material shaped as a disk. Information is holographically stored throughout the volume of the thick disk using angle (θ) [2] or wavelength (λ) multiplexing [3]. By tuning either the wavelength or the angle of the reference beam, multiple holograms of data blocks are superimposed at each location. The stored data is retrieved by using the disk/head motion to address a desired location and then selecting the angle or wavelength of the reconstructing beam to retrieve any one block of data. The system shown in Fig. 1 is an angle multiplexed system with an acousto-optic device used to to rapidly select the angle of illumination.

articleTitle: Tolerance Study Of Pulse Erasure In A High Density Magneto-optic Disk Drive
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Pulse erasure technique is used in a high-density MO disk drive to minimize partial erasure on adjacent tracks. However, a system jitter can introduce a relative delay between the erase pulse and the write pulse (erase/write delay), resulting in an undesirable erasure residue. A larger erase power and/or longer erase pulse width are needed to ensure a residue-& erasure. It is thus of interest to study the effects of erase power, linear velocity, and erase/write delay on the pulse erasure residue.

articleTitle: Fidelity And Throughput Limitations In Page-oriented Volume Holographic Optical Data Storage
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Volume Holographic optical memories provide the potential for very high density, rapid parallel access data storage. Recent advances in spatial light modulators (SLMs), storage materials, and detector arrays have increased the possibility of volume holographic memory implementation. However, despite these advances in technology, several fundamental issues remain unresolved. These include the accuracy with which stored digital data can be read back from volume holograms and the optical throughput that is achievable. Throughput is defined as the fraction of the readout beam intensity that is diffracted into the desired signal beam. The throughput and fidelity directly determine the achievable SNR, which impacts the viability and capacity of volume holographic storage. In this paper we examine quantitatively the throughput and fidelity achievable in a common implementation of a volume holographic memory (shown schematically in Fig. l.)

articleTitle: High Density Magneto-optical Recording With A SHG Green Laser
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Recording with a light source of shorter wavelength and a high NA objective lens is essential to realize optical data storage at high areal density. Laser-diode pumped Nd:YAG SHG green lasers offer this potential. We have developed a high power green laser and a low noise GdFeCo/lbFeCo MO disk for the wavelength of 532 nm. With a newly designed optical pick-up and an objective lens of 0.6 NA, a C/N ratio > 48 dB was obtained for mark length ?f 0.45 μm.

articleTitle: Comparison Of Polarization Wadout Techniques For Magneto-optic Systems
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The information recorded on a magneto-optic (MO) disk is read out by sensing the polarization state of the light beam reflected from the disk. Optimizing the detection of the reflected beam's polarization state is critical to maximize the signal-to-noise ratio in a magneto-optic disk drive.1 Examples of differential detection schemes that are capable of correcting for the ellipticity in the reflected beam and maximizing the common mode noise rejection are shown in Fig. 1. With the method of Jones calculus,a the detection system can be optimized for a given head media interface by specifying the retardance of the liquid crystal variable retarder (LCVR) in case (a) or the general waveplate in case (b) and the angles for the other optical components.

articleTitle: Optical Data Storage Using Persistent Spectral Hole Burning
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The use of holography is attractive for optical data storage due to its poten­tial for implementing page oriented data storage systems. However, multiplexed recording using Bragg selective materials has not provided a large enough stor­age capability to justify the expense of these systems. Persistent spectral hole burning holography allows multiplexed recording using much smaller wavelength separations between the holograms, and hence dramatically increases the storage capacity possible in holographic memory systems [1]. A comparison between the wavelength selectivity obtained for transmission gratings recorded using hole burning in a dye doped polymer film versus Bragg selectivity in a 1 cm thick iron-doped lithium niobate crystal is shown in Fig. (1).

articleTitle: Compact Optical Light Paths
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The primary function of an optical pickup is twofold: focusing the laser light using a high-quality objective lens into a diffraction-limited spot on the information layer of the disc and detecting the changes in the reflected light due to the layer's microstructure. Two other important functions of the pickup are the generation of the focus- and tracking-error signals [I]. The light reflected from the disc is partly coupled to a detector by a beamsplitter. The reliability of the detected signals is mainly determined by the mutual positional stability of the laser, beamsplitter and detector. This stability can be improved by putting these components close together. Another critical component in an optical recorder or player concerning its positional stability is the focusing and tracking actuator. An improved stability may be achieved by integrating the whole optical pickup together with the actuator in one device. In this paper we distinguish three kinds of applications for optical pickups: read-only systems, systems for recording and/or erasing in phase-change, ablative or dye materials, and Magneto-Optical (MO) players.

articleTitle: A New Tracking Method For Helical Scanning Optical Tape Recorder
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: In various scanning methods for-recording on and reproducing information from an optical tape[1]-[2], helical scanning has the merit of achieving a high scanning speed using a compact mechanism. With helical scanning, however, it is difficult to track pit streams because the tracking pattern is difficult to preformat on a thin tape, and this influences the precision of the track pitches and the S/N of the reproduced tracking error. Another disadvantage is that there is no signal when the tape is not wrapped around the drum, which causes track jumping at the starting point of scanning, so it is impossible to reproduce data track by track. We have solved these problems using a high precision drum motor, a high SNR organic dye-polymer tape, and a new tracking method. In this summary, we will outline the HS-OTR (Helical Scanning Optical Tape Recorder)'s hardware and tracking system.

articleTitle: A Recording Experiment With Rotating Optical Head For Magneto-optical Tape Recording System
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: We are developing a magneto-optical tape recording system for HDTV and future TV systems because they need an extremely large capacity memory for video files. It is necessary to employ a rotating scanning optical head in order to record high data transfer rate signals such as HDTV. Among the configurations of rotating optical heads, we selected the head configuration which divides the optics into the fixed part and the rotating part, and in which focusing and tracking control are carried out with the actuator in the fixed part because it is possible to minimize the rotating optics. However, in this configuration, there is a drawback that the focusing operation makes the focused spot characteristics worse. In this report, we introduce a configuration of the rotating optical head that eliminates the drawback and recording experiments using the rotating optical head.

articleTitle: Thin Optical Head With Flip-chip Bonded Module For CD-ROM Drives
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The use of CD-ROMs has grown enormously in recent years as they have become a favored media for electronic books and software applications, and this has created a great demand for more compact optical heads for CD-ROM drives. In an attempt to improve upon previous efforts at greater compactness), authors developed a compact optical module which integrated a laser diode chip, a photodiode chip, and a holographic optical element, and which could be combined with an objective lens and an actuator to produce a compact optical head). This paper describes a further improvement in compactness achieved using a new flip-chip bonded module design. Optical module size is 6mm(W)x6mm(D)x1.64mm (H), its weight is 0.25g, and head thickness is less than 7mm, including the objective lens working distance.

articleTitle: High Speed Access Mechanism For 90mm 1 " Height Optical Disk Drive
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: An optical disk drive configuration using a galvano-mirror as a tracking actuator mounted on a non-movable part of the separated optical system is preferable to achieve high speed access, low power consumption and compact low profile. The hysteresis characteristics and temperature dependence of the galvano-mirror that affects the tracking and the access performance have left much to be solved. This paper describes a 90mm 1" height optical disk drive mechanism using a newly developed galvano-mirror that was improved these intrinsic issues.

articleTitle: Recording Characteristics And Reliability Of Novel Writable-cd Using A Au-Sn Alloy Single Layer
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Over the past few years, some studies have been made on write-once type writable- CD<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1)-3)</sup>. This writable-CD has attracted a great deal of interest due to compatibility with conventional CD. This has been realized by means of double layered structure, dye recording layer and Au reflective layer. This has, however, disadvantages of degradation of dye layer by sun light irradiation and rapid drop of reflectance with a little decrease of wavelength. To solve these problems, we introduce novel writable-CD using Au-Sn alloy. This has advantages of single layered simple structure, low toxicity and high tolerance to sun light.

articleTitle: The Poincari Sphere Description Of Magneto-optic Read Out
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The data signal used in Magneto-optic disk drives is based on detecting changes in the polarization state of light reflected from the disk. This change is small and often must be detected in the presence of birefringence in the disk substrate and retardation in the read out optics. The mathematics used to model the propagation of light through the optical system does not typically produce intuition or insight. The Poincare sphere description provides a graphic representation of the polarization state on the surface of the sphere as well as a set of rules for transforming the polarization state as it interacts with various system components. This visualization develops intuition and provides a conceptual tool for understanding the behavior of system components and their effects on system performance. This paper will illustrate the evolution of the polarization state through an MO system by the use of the Poincare sphere

articleTitle: Optimum Reflectivity Design Of Laser Diode Facets And A Recording Medium For An Integrated Flying Optical Head
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: A very small integrated flying optical head has been proposed and high-quality read and write performance have been demonstrated with a phase change recording medium. The reflectivities of the laser diode attached to the slider and the reflectivity of the medium strongly affect the head performance. This paper describes the reflectivity design of the head and evaluates its performance.

articleTitle: Diffraction Pattern From Magneto-optical Edges
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Mark edge recording and short wavelength sources have been examined as a technique of higher density capacity in magneto-optical (MO) disks. Although various methods for reducing the intersymbol interference in the high density MO disks have been proposed, few schemes have been made on the optical edge detection system of the MO disks. We have studied a MO edge readout system which optically processes diffraction wavefronts from the phase edges within a diffraction limited spot, and detects edges from their intensity distributions. The edge detection utilizes characteristics of the MO edges that behave as the phase edges with phase shift of 0 and π radians to the Ken components of the reflected light.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties And R/W Characteristics Of Exchanie-coupled Double-layered MO Nedia Using GdFeCo/TbFeTi Film
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: We have developed a 200 mm MO disc with an exchange-coupled double-layered filmCl1 for a high performance media. In t h i s paper, magnetic properties and R/W characteristics are reported and discussed.

articleTitle: Applications For Optical Storage
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Optical storage libraries are available for all levels of data processing; large mainframes, intermediate workstations, and personal computers on local area networks. Interest in these libraries is large and growing. While there are several attributes which make optical libraries attractive, by far the most significant is the relative cost of on-line storage (relative to traditional magnetic disks). Other attributes which sometimes make optical storage desirable are also discussed along with attributes which work against optical storage libraries. Many applicatioris find optical storage desirable. Some are unique in that they were not commonly done before optical storage became available. Others have been around for a long time using other storage media.

articleTitle: Conference Digest. Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993 [Front Matter and Table of Contents]
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: Presents the front matter and table of contents from the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Joint International Symposium on Optical Memory and Optical Data Storage 1993
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.
